title: From Recovery to Drop-off: How Action Post-training Reduces a VLM's Late-Layer Depth Decodability
action_head: flow/diffusion action expert (cross-attends to backbone KV); backbone was earlier trained on DCT-BPE discrete action tokens, then fully fine-tuned on LIBERO with insulation released
methods: windowed zero-ablation of MLP vs attention writes
probing accumulated MLP writes vs residual stream
question: How much of a VLM's depth (spatiogeometric) information stays decodable after action post-training into a VLA, where in the stack is it lost, and which module causes the loss?
key_findings: Floor: the VLA decodes depth worse than its weight-matched VLM at all 36 layers; band means d1 early 0.705 vs 0.617, mid 0.701 vs 0.606, late 0.744 vs 0.578 (Table 2); narrowest gap ~0.04 at L20.
Cliff: from L28 to L35 the VLM rises +0.040 d1 while the VLA falls -0.123; final layer 0.752 (VLM) vs 0.506 (VLA), a 0.246 gap (Table 2).

Zeroing the VLA's MLP writes in L33-35 raises final-layer d1 from 0.506 to 0.584 (+0.078, 'majority of the 0.123 cliff'); attention ablation in the same window gives +0.031; the same MLP ablation in the base VLM gives +0.015 (Table 3).

Accumulated MLP writes are more depth-decodable than the residual stream in the base VLM (d1 ~0.80-0.84 vs 0.66-0.75); in the VLA these deposits collapse from ~0.68 to 0.38 over the final blocks, and ridge SNR falls to ~0.03 by the last layer.
Residual-stream norm is 100-1000x a single MLP write in the first two-thirds of the stack and ~10x late, offered as the reason late writes can reshape the stream.

evidence.setting: offline dataset only (LIBERO frames; no rollouts)
benchmarks: LIBERO frames (primary + wrist views), Depth-Anything-3 pseudo-labels
evidence.scale: n = 400 rollout-strided LIBERO frames (Table 4), 25% held out by rollout; one 41.8M-parameter DPT probe per model-layer cell; 2 x 2 x 12 ablation design; single seed
evidence.statistics: no: single-seed probes and ablations, no CIs or tests; authors explicitly rely on the structure of the dissociation rather than per-cell significance
evidence.baselines: weight-matched base VLM as reference; attention ablation and base-VLM ablation as controls

causal_validation: Yes at representation level: zeroing late MLP writes increases final-layer depth decodability (+0.078 d1) with attention and base-VLM controls. The outcome is probe decodability with a freshly trained probe per condition, not model behavior.
closed_loop: No. Authors state they make no claim that the ablations improve closed-loop policy behavior; nothing is measured on actions.
limitations_stated: One VLM-VLA pair on one dataset (LIBERO).
One DPT probe class, corroborated only by ridge regression.
Targets are Depth-Anything-3 pseudo-ground-truth, affine-aligned, not metric depth.
Depth is necessary but not sufficient for spatial understanding.
Causal claims are representation-level and single-seed; no closed-loop claim.
The whole post-training pipeline (data and three stages) is a bundled treatment.
critique: Ablating MLP writes in L33-35 yields d1 0.584, close to the VLA's own L32 value (0.576 in Table 5). The 'recovery' may just restore the pre-cliff state, not reveal 'interference'. Late layers re-formatting for action output would show the same pattern; the interference framing is stronger than the evidence.

Only 400 frames to train a 41.8M-parameter probe per layer, single seed: layer-to-layer differences of a few hundredths of d1 (e.g. +0.015 vs +0.031) may be within probe noise, and no variance estimate is given.

Lower depth decodability in the last layers of a policy is not obviously a defect: no behavioral link (e.g. depth-sensitive task failures) is shown, so the result says nothing yet about whether the policy uses depth.

Nice design point: the weight-matched pair is a cleaner contrast than most retention papers. But since LIBERO fine-tuning releases the insulation, the result may not transfer to insulated pi0.5-style models.
one_line: In a weight-matched Molmo2-ER / MolmoAct2 pair, action post-training makes depth less decodable at every layer and sharply so in the last 8 layers, and zeroing the last MLP writes undoes most of that terminal drop.
